To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a space warp operator that warps a 3D surface or volume may be specified in realtime, using a 6 Do F magnetic tracker in each of two hands, by simultaneously displacing and rotating two or more points on the surface or volume.
(i) A 3D space warp can be specified in terms a set of point-displacement and point-rotation constraints.

(1) a new formalism for interpolating a set of point-displacement and orientation constraints is presented, and (2) it is used to implement an intuitive two-handed interface that allows realtime creation of 3D free-form deformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new deformation operator, Twister, which allows the simultaneous interpolation of two sets of constraints: 6 displacement constraints, and 6 rotational constraints.
the development and application of a novel two-handed direct manipulation interface for the freeform deformation of 3D models.
the design and implementation of a 3D shape editing system based on the Twister space-warp operator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper introduces a new approach to free-form deformations that adds the capability to specify and interpolate rotational constraints, and that it is implemented as a two-handed direct manipulation tool that is intuitive and effective for the editing of 3-dimensional shapes.
Twister provides a powerful and intuitive two-handed interface for the interactive editing of 3-D shapes.
Twister is a new and useful technique for 3D free-form deformation that provides an intuitive and effective two-hand interface for the interactive editing of shapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the first two-handed, direct manipulation interface for free-form deformation that allows the user to simultaneously specify both point displacements and rotations, and to apply the deformation to the shape in realtime.
we have introduced the concept of a space-warp that interpolates both point displacements and rotations, and that it can be applied to 3D shapes using a two-handed interface.
we have developed a novel 3D deformation method that can be used for 3D shape manipulation and editing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a space warp can simultaneously interpolate a number of constraints that are not all of the same type, in this case, point displacements and rotations.
a 2D space warp, such as the 3D twist deformation, may be extended to a 3D space warp, by adding a rotational component.
the space-warp formalism can be used to interpolate multiple constraints of arbitrary type.
